How therapy may work

Methods with a purpose

Understand what an approach emphasizes and who uses it.

Training and use vary by clinician. Profiles and direct confirmation remain the source of truth.

Cognitive Behavioral Therapy

A structured approach that explores connections among thoughts, emotions, and behavior.

Published by Kody Evans, Dr. Taylor Nolan, Emily Johnsrud, Gary Ashley, Sonia Hassan

Dialectical Behavior Therapy Skills

Skills-oriented work that may support mindfulness, emotional regulation, distress tolerance, and relationships.

Published by Kody Evans, Emily Johnsrud, Sonia Hassan

Emotionally Focused Therapy

An attachment-informed approach often used to understand emotional patterns and strengthen connection.

Published by Kody Evans

Gottman Method Informed Therapy

Relationship work informed by research on friendship, conflict, repair, trust, and shared meaning.

Published by Kody Evans, Dr. Taylor Nolan, Gary Ashley

Internal Family Systems Informed Therapy

An approach that can help clients relate to different internal experiences with greater curiosity and compassion.

Published by Kody Evans

Solution Focused Brief Therapy

A goal-oriented approach that notices strengths, exceptions, resources, and practical next steps.

Published by Kody Evans

Narrative Therapy

An approach that separates people from problems and examines the stories shaping identity and possibility.

Published by Kody Evans, Sonia Hassan

Motivational Interviewing

A collaborative approach for exploring ambivalence, values, motivation, and personally meaningful change.

Published by Kody Evans, Gary Ashley, Sonia Hassan

Attachment Based Therapy

Therapy informed by how early and current relationships can influence safety, connection, and response patterns.

Published by Kody Evans, Emily Johnsrud

Family Systems Therapy

An approach that considers relationships, roles, patterns, and context rather than isolating one person as the problem.

Published by Kody Evans, Emily Johnsrud

Mindfulness Based Therapy

Practices that may help clients notice internal experiences and respond with greater awareness and choice.

Published by Kody Evans

Trauma Informed Therapy

Care organized around safety, choice, collaboration, trust, and sensitivity to the effects of difficult experiences.

Ask which clinicians currently use this approach.
